system_description.narrative_title: Converging Wars, AI Arms Race, and Energy Strain in a Fragile Geo‑Economic Order
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is being reshaped by simultaneous shocks: regional wars tied to Iran and Russia-Ukraine that are widening into maritime and energy chokepoints; an overheated, capital‑intensive AI and data‑centre boom that is creating financial, cyber and industrial stresses; and volatile macro policy as central banks confront inflation and bond‑market signals. Great‑power tech rivalry (China‑US) and domestic political turbulence (US, India, Israel) are amplifying cross‑market contagion, leaving a tightly coupled global order more sensitive to policy missteps and supply‑chain disruptions.
system_description.scope: States and alliances, regional conflicts and maritime chokepoints (Middle East, Red Sea, Hormuz), global energy and commodity flows, international financial markets and central banks, major tech firms and the AI/data‑centre ecosystem, global supply chains, international institutions and sanctions regimes, and domestic political pressures that influence foreign policy.
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic‑security order (interconnected international system of states, markets, technology ecosystems and institutions).
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East regional security and maritime trade chokepoints
Global financial markets and central banking regimes

variables.name: US–Iran regional conflict
variables.description: An escalating military confrontation between Iran, the United States and regional proxies that is spreading strikes across the Middle East and imperiling maritime security and energy transport.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and economic coercion
variables.description: A protracted war in which Ukraine is expanding asymmetric strikes on Russian logistics and industry while Western governments coordinate arms, sanctions and economic pressure on Moscow.

variables.name: US–China tech and AI rivalry
variables.description: A broad strategic contest between the United States and China over AI, advanced semiconductors, data‑center buildout and export controls that is reshaping supply chains, investment and industrial policy.

variables.name: Global monetary and bond-market stress
variables.description: Divergent central‑bank policies—centred on the U.S. Fed—and a sharp repricing of bond yields are driving market volatility, credit risks and cross‑border capital flows.

variables.name: Renewed US trade protectionism
variables.description: A wave of U.S. tariffs and trade measures is forcing trading partners and multinational firms to reconfigure supply chains, investment decisions and trade alliances.
